main_body: Grey stove: a light blue-grey top plate (rows 9-12) with two small dark knobs, above a tall dark-grey front panel (rows 14-29) with an inset black firebox opening showing flame.
top_band: light blue-grey #a0acb8 rows 9-11, with a lighter #d0d8e0 edge line at row 12; a 3-4 row band that is sharply lighter than the face, but it reads as a plate or lid band on a front-on body
evidence: Column x=8 reads: outline row 8, light band rows 9-11 (L=170), bright edge line row 12 (L=215), dark shadow row 13, then the front face rows 14-29 (L=82) with a black firebox inset (rows 18-25). So the top is a 3-row lighter band with a front-edge line and an eave shadow, over a 16-row front face with a recessed opening. That is close to the guide's green cabinet (top 5 + edge + eave), but the top is only 3 rows, and the band is a flat plate with knobs that looks like a vertical panel seen straight on. The body is also very tall and narrow, and the top is barely deeper than a cap line. Borderline; the construction checks are met on paper, but the top is thin and reads as a front-on plate, so I fail it strictly.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The front panel (L=82) and the firebox (L=19) are large flat areas of one colour. The 0% flat-fill figure only reflects the grid-like checker of the panel, not real texture. 60% of dark edge pixels are neutral, which leans towards a near-black outline and makes a sticker-like look. The flame has a nice gradient, but the body has no grain, rivets or per-pixel variation, so it is thinner and flatter than the references.
